subject: Post-call: deployment pathway and dedicated GPU mix for Astra Logistics
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call: deployment pathway and dedicated GPU mix for Astra Logistics

Hi Lucas/Tara,

Thanks again for taking time today to walk through Astra's inference needs. Short recap and recommended next steps below.

Call recap (30 min):
- Primary use: real-time document routing + short summarization + occasional long-form extraction.
- Traffic shape: spiky peaks during EOD and batch ingestion windows; need low p95 for interactive flows.
- Compliance: audit logs + VPC peering for production; Hosted API ok for initial POC, but Private VPC may be required longer-term depending on procurement.

Recommendation (initial): evaluate Dedicated capacity with a blended GPU pool.
- Why: predictable throughput under spiky load and ability to tune latency vs cost via an H100/A100 mix.
- H100 nodes for low-latency, long-context requests; A100 (or queued batch on same fleet) for higher-throughput cheaper batches.

Clarifying asks to size a starter Dedicated config:
1) Confirm peak TPS (requests/sec) and average TPS during normal hours.
2) Share token mix / histogram (percent of requests under 64 tokens, 64–512, >512) or a sample prompt set.
3) Latency SLOs (p50/p95) and whether p95 under 350ms is a hard requirement.
4) Any hard compliance/timeframes that push toward Private deployment vs Hosted/Dedicated.

Attached: capacity_workbook_v1.xlsx (starter worksheet) and a short compliance checklist.
Next steps:
- If you can send token histograms, we’ll run a quick cost/throughput model and propose a 2–3 node Dedicated starter (H100+ A100 blend) and an optional Private plan.
- I’ll propose two POC tracks: (A) 2-week Dedicated capacity trial; (B) Hosted POC for feature validation (faster, lower commitment).

Available times for a short follow-up to review the worksheet: Thu 10th 11:00–12:00 PT or Fri 11th 09:30–11:00 PT. Pick one and I’ll send a calendar invite.

—
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer

Thanks Neha — helpful recap.

Quick answers:
- Peak TPS (user-facing): ~50 req/s during peak 30-min window (spikes up to ~70 for short bursts); average during day ~12–18 req/s.
- Token mix: ~60% short (<64 tokens), ~30% mid (64–512), ~10% long (512–2k). Long requests are heavier extraction jobs.
- Latency: p95 ~<350ms is desired for the interactive flows; for batch/extraction we can tolerate higher.
- Compliance: we need VPC peering for production; initial proof-of-concept can run on Hosted or Dedicated depending on cost.

Budget/timeframe: we’d like to evaluate a Dedicated POC in Jan; procurement would need a simple SOW/estimate. Can you indicate an expected starting SKU estimate and whether H100 is necessary vs A100 only?

Lucas
Director, ML Engineering
Astra Logistics

Lucas — thanks for the quick numbers, that helps. A few sizing notes and a starter configuration we typically recommend for this mix of short+long tokens and spiky traffic: 

Assumptions from your numbers: peak 50–70 TPS, average ~15 TPS, token mix as you shared, p95 target ~350ms for interactive.

Starter Dedicated proposal (rough):
- Blended pool: 2 x H100 (low-latency, long-context requests) + 1 x A100 (background batch/queued inference).
  - Reasoning: H100 gives ~2–3x latency headroom for long-context autoregressive workloads and larger batch single-request throughput; A100 is cost-efficient for bursty queued requests and mid-sized prompts.
- Concurrency + batching guidance: configure per-model concurrency cap of 8 on H100 nodes with continuous batching window ~8–12ms to preserve p95; A100 can have higher batching window (20–40ms) and higher concurrency for throughput.
- KV cache: enable prefix/KV caching for repeated short prompts (expected 60% of requests) to cut token compute and reduce latency.
- Autoscale policy: keep a minimum of 1 H100 and scale to 2 H100 at sustained >30 TPS for interactive; A100 pool scales based on queued latency and queued-depth thresholds.

Estimated starting SKU (very rough):
- If we map to vendor instance types: 2x H100 nodes + 1x A100 node (reserved for POC) — we’ll provide cost gamma in the workbook. We’ll also run model-specific benchmarks once you share a sample prompt set.

Deliverables we’ll prepare once we have the histogram/sample set:
1) Model-level latency and tokens/sec estimates (p50/p95) for your prompt set.
2) Cost/throughput tradeoff table (H100-only vs blended H100+A100 vs A100-only).
3) POC plan and SOW draft for procurement (2-week Dedicated trial).

Attaching a quick CSV with the prototype SKU estimate for your procurement team to review.
